areas.summary: Homes are the biggest thing most people buy, so fake listings and money scams do real harm. Spare Home checks owners, watches for scams, moderates listings to published rules and logs every removal in public.

features.name: Stop fake listings
features.does: Trust that every live listing was placed by a checked owner of a real home.

parts.name: Home scam patterns
parts.what: Researches home-sale scams, such as seller impersonation, fake listings and deposit redirection, and feeds them into the kit's research on scam methods (KIT-A10-F12-P1).

parts.name: Fake listing checks
parts.what: Flags photos reused without a recorded licence, prices far below the market and details that do not match the record, for review, as Home rules on the kit's listing checks. They feed the kit's fraud signals (KIT-A10-F12-P2) once the kit builds them.

parts.name: Same home listed twice
parts.what: Catches the same property listed twice, whether by a co-owner, an agent or a scammer, and holds the newer listing for review.

features.name: Avoid money scams
features.does: Get clear warnings about deposit and bank detail scams at every step where money is mentioned.

parts.name: Warnings wherever money comes up
parts.what: Shows a plain warning about deposit and bank detail scams at every step where money comes up, such as offers, the lawyers' workspace and settlement, and pinned in every sale chat. It adds the kit's scam warnings in chat (KIT-A8-F9-P1) once the kit builds them.

features.name: Report a listing or a person
features.does: Report a listing, message or person and see what happened to your report.

parts.name: Home report reasons
parts.what: Adds home-sale report reasons to the kit's report forms and tells the reporter the outcome.

features.name: Moderate listings fairly
features.does: Have listings checked against published rules, with every removal and its reason logged in public.

parts.name: Listing rules
parts.what: Published rules on what listings may say and show, such as no discrimination, no misleading claims and no one else's private details.

parts.name: Listing moderation settings
parts.what: Sends reports and flagged listings to the kit's moderation queue with Home's listing rules attached to each case.

parts.name: Listing appeals
parts.what: Lets a seller appeal a removal to a member panel through the kit's appeals.

features.name: Keep people's privacy
features.does: Hide your exact address until a viewing is booked, keep it private when the home is empty, and keep visitors' and neighbours' details private.

parts.name: Address hiding
parts.what: Uses the kit's approximate location to show only the street or suburb until a checked buyer books a viewing, if the seller chooses.

parts.name: Hide that a home is empty
parts.what: Never shows that a home is empty, that the owner is overseas or that it is a deceased estate unless the seller chooses, offers to show open home times only to registered buyers, and warns before going live if photos show an alarm panel, key safe or keys.

features.name: Rate the right things
features.does: Rate professionals after a job, while buyers and sellers are never publicly scored.

parts.name: What can be rated
parts.what: Sets that only professionals' services are rated, and that buyers and sellers are not given public scores.

features.name: Report reused photos or plans
features.does: As a photographer, architect or other rights owner, report a listing that uses your photos or plans without permission.

parts.name: Rights owner notices
parts.what: Adds Home's per-file licence records to the kit's copyright notices, so a rights owner can report a copied photo or plan, such as an earlier agent's campaign photos or an architect's plans, and the seller can answer with the licence on record.

areas.name: Law, the agency line and countries
areas.summary: Spare Home must stay a set of tools and never become an unlicensed agent. This area turns the law into product rules: agency law, anti-money-laundering, overseas buyers, privacy, consumer law and each country's own rules.

features.name: Stay on the right side of agency law
features.does: Use every tool knowing Spare Home never negotiates, advises on price or acts for anyone in the sale.

parts.name: Where tools end and agency begins
parts.what: What the app may and may not do under real estate law, with sources and a lawyer's view, for every tool that does more than publish an advert, such as offers, the buyer register, viewings and AI replies.

parts.name: Agency guardrails
parts.what: Product rules that stop the app, its staff and its AI tools from negotiating, recommending offers or advising on price for a seller.

parts.name: Legal sign-off
parts.what: A lawyer's review of the guardrails and the wording on every screen that touches offers or price.

parts.name: A fallback for each tool
parts.what: Keeps a ready fallback, behind the kit's feature switches, for each tool HM01 might find to be agency work: offers kept to a register only, the buyer register and multi-offer run only through a booked fixed-fee licensed agent (HOME-A12-F4), or the tool switched off.

features.name: Meet anti-money-laundering law
features.does: Have identity checks done by the people the law requires, such as lawyers, with Spare Home doing only its own share.

parts.name: Is Spare Home a reporting entity
parts.what: Finds whether Spare Home has anti-money-laundering duties of its own, on top of the kit's anti-money-laundering programme, and what lawyers and agents must check.

parts.name: Sharing checks with lawyers
parts.what: Lets a person share their identity check result with their lawyer, with consent, to save repeating it.

features.name: Know the rules for overseas buyers
features.does: As a buyer, learn early whether you may need consent to buy and which statement your lawyer needs.

parts.name: Overseas buyer rules
parts.what: Sets out who may buy residential land without consent and the statement every buyer gives their lawyer.

parts.name: Overseas buyer notice
parts.what: Shows buyers plain information about these rules on listings and offers, without judging their case.

features.name: Have your privacy protected
features.does: Know what Spare Home keeps about you, why, for how long, and ask to see or correct it.

parts.name: Privacy impact assessment
parts.what: A privacy impact assessment for Spare Home under NZ privacy law, done before launch, including the notice duty for details collected from someone else (IPP 3A, since 1 May 2026), redone for each new country, and added to the kit's register of assessments (KIT-A18-F10-P1) once that exists.

parts.name: How long data is kept
parts.what: Sets how long each kind of Home data is kept after a sale, carried out by the kit's retention schedules.

parts.name: Privacy request clock
parts.what: Adds Home's data to the kit's privacy page and tracks the legal reply time in working days on the kit's working days and notice periods.

parts.name: Notices for details from others
parts.what: Tells people whose details Spare Home got from someone else, such as tenants named by a seller, owners and co-owners on the title, partners on a shared shortlist and lawyers named by a party, as IPP 3A requires.

features.name: Trust that listings follow consumer law
features.does: Rely on listings that avoid misleading claims and discrimination.

parts.name: Consumer and advertising law
parts.what: Adds the home-sale questions to the kit's consumer law for platforms: who is in trade in a private sale, the platform's own duties, and human rights rules for listings.

parts.name: Listing wording checks
parts.what: Flags wording in listings that may mislead or discriminate before it goes live.

features.name: Keep each country's rules in a pack
features.does: Sell under rules kept in a country pack, starting with New Zealand, so a new country is added without rewriting the app.

parts.name: Rules-pack format for home sales
parts.what: Home's layer on the kit's NZ country pack, in a format able to hold required listing facts such as the UK's material information Parts A, B and C, disclosures, energy certificates, methods of sale, price display and underquoting rules, cooling-off periods, redress scheme membership, notary-led conveyancing, deeds registries as well as title registers, working-day rules, time zones for deadlines and auctions, and the agency line. It moves onto the kit's country packs (KIT-A19-F6-P1) when they are built.

parts.name: New Zealand rules pack
parts.what: The first pack, there from day one, holding NZ disclosures, price display and GST labels, tenancy rules, methods of sale including 'enquiries over', and the agreement's working-day rules, so no NZ rule is hard-coded.

features.name: Agree to clear terms
features.does: Read short, plain terms and confirm what you declare as a seller.

parts.name: Terms of use
parts.what: Plain terms for sellers, buyers and professionals, written by a lawyer and kept in the kit's terms and policy versions.

parts.name: Seller declaration
parts.what: A declaration the seller makes that they may sell and that their facts and disclosures are true.

parts.name: Professional indemnity cover
parts.what: Adds professional indemnity cover for Home's guides, disclosure checklist, price guide and due date engine to the kit's co-op insurance, which lists only directors and officers, cyber and public liability cover, with the limits the terms state.

features.name: Prepare the first other countries
features.does: Know that the rules-pack format has been tested against Australia's states and the UK before any country after NZ is added.

parts.name: First other countries
parts.what: Researches the rules for Australia's states and the UK as the first packs after NZ, to test the rules-pack format before it is fixed.

features.name: See when a seller is in trade
features.does: As a buyer, see when a seller sells homes in trade, such as a developer or investor.

parts.name: Trader status for sellers
parts.what: Asks whether a seller sells homes in trade and shows buyers the trader details the kit keeps, if the Commerce Commission's guidance on traders on platforms covers land listings (unverified).

areas.name: Access for everyone: accessibility, languages, phones and offline
areas.summary: Anyone should be able to sell or buy, whatever their abilities, language, device or signal. Spare Home works with screen readers, in many languages, as an installed phone app, and offline where it matters most.

features.name: Use it with any ability
features.does: Use every screen with a screen reader, keyboard, zoom or switch device.

parts.name: Home screens to the access standard
parts.what: Builds every Home screen to WCAG 2.2 AA from the kit's accessible components.

parts.name: Room-aware photo descriptions
parts.what: Uses the kit's image descriptions, adding room names from the plan, for the seller to check so blind buyers know what is shown.

parts.name: Accessibility testing
parts.what: Tests with disabled users and tools before each release.

parts.name: Accessible documents
parts.what: Makes brochures, disclosure statements, plans and watermarked copies as tagged, accessible PDFs.

features.name: Use it in your language
features.does: Use Spare Home in English and te reo Māori, and find places typed with or without macrons.

parts.name: Home words in translation files
parts.what: Keeps every Home word on screen in the kit's translation framework.

parts.name: Te reo Māori
parts.what: A full te reo Māori version, written with fluent speakers.

parts.name: Place names with or without macrons
parts.what: Uses the kit's macron-aware matching for suburbs, streets and school zones in Home search and addresses.

features.name: Install it on your phone
features.does: Install Spare Home on a phone and get notifications, without needing a big download.

parts.name: Home in the phone app
parts.what: Puts Spare Home in the installable phone app the co-op chooses for all marketplaces.

features.name: Keep working offline
features.does: Draft a listing, check in open home visitors and read saved homes with no signal.

parts.name: Offline work
parts.what: Keeps drafts, the open home register and saved homes on the device and syncs when back online.

features.name: Choose how you are told
features.does: Choose which updates reach you, and by push, email or text.

parts.name: Home notification events
parts.what: Adds Home's events, such as new offers and due dates, to the kit's notification settings, with quiet hours.

features.name: Use it on slow connections
features.does: Browse and list on a slow or costly connection with a low data mode.

parts.name: Low data mode
parts.what: Serves smaller images and holds back video unless asked.

features.name: See your own units and formats
features.does: See areas, money, dates and addresses the way your country writes them.

parts.name: Home units and formats
parts.what: Uses the kit's local formats for areas, money, dates and addresses and adds land units such as hectares.

features.name: Work offline on site
features.does: Show listing facts and chosen documents at the door, run the pre-settlement inspection and draw a floor plan with no signal.

parts.name: More offline on site
parts.what: Adds the chosen documents, the pre-settlement inspection checklist and the plan drawer to Home's one offline store (HOME-A17-F4-P1), which already holds drafts, the open home register and saved homes.

features.name: Read guides the easy way
features.does: Read easy-read versions of the selling and buying guides, and watch the video guides in NZ Sign Language.

parts.name: Easy-read guides
parts.what: Easy-read versions of the selling and buying guides.

parts.name: NZ Sign Language video guides
parts.what: NZ Sign Language versions of the video guides.

features.name: Read listings in your language
features.does: Read listings and messages translated into your language, and use Spare Home in more community languages.

parts.name: Listing translation
parts.what: Translates listings on request on the kit's machine translation at cost, and messages through the kit's message translation, labelled as machine translated.

parts.name: The original wording counts
parts.what: Labels translated listings and disclosures with a note that the seller's original wording is the one that counts.

parts.name: First community languages
parts.what: Early translations of Home's screens into Chinese, Hindi, Samoan and Tongan, written with fluent speakers.

features.name: Read scanned documents with a screen reader
features.does: Have scanned council reports, titles and older reports read by a screen reader.

parts.name: Text layer for scanned documents
parts.what: Adds a text layer to scanned documents in the vault, such as land information reports, titles and older consents, using an open text recognition engine, marked as machine read so the original scan stays the record.

areas.name: Your data, AI and plugins
areas.summary: Members own their data and can take it with them, even in the middle of a sale. Everything a person can do, an AI agent or script can do through the same commands, inside the same agency guardrails, and a person confirms every high-risk command.

features.name: Export everything
features.does: Download your listing, photos, plans, documents, messages and payments in open formats.

parts.name: Home export contents
parts.what: Adds Home data to the kit's data export: JSON for data, PDF for documents, and the original photos and plans.

parts.name: Export screen
parts.what: Lets a person start a Home export from the kit's privacy page and download it when ready.

parts.name: Take a live sale elsewhere
parts.what: Hands a live listing to a licensed agent or another site in an open listing format, passing on buyer register entries only for buyers who consent.

features.name: Delete your data
features.does: Delete your account and data, except what the law says must be kept.

parts.name: Home data deletion
parts.what: Adds Home's data and keeping rules to the kit's account deletion, erases personal details in the offer register, the record of who was told what and the public change history by the kit's method while those logs stay intact, and explains anything kept and for how long.

parts.name: What stays public after deletion
parts.what: Decides what happens to a home's public price history, days on market and published sale price when the seller deletes their account.

features.name: Script any action
features.does: Do anything the app can do through its command interface.

parts.name: Home command set
parts.what: Defines every Home action as a kit operation with a published schema, used by screens, AI and plugins alike.

parts.name: Open listing data
parts.what: Publishes live public listings as open, read-only data, leaving out hidden addresses, private and coming-soon listings, the owner's identity and media the licence forbids, with rate limits and terms against bulk scraping.

features.name: Use an AI assistant
features.does: Let an AI assistant draft a listing, sort photos, summarise documents or track dates, within the same limits as a person.

parts.name: AI access
parts.what: Exposes the Home commands to AI agents through the kit's MCP server, with the person's own permissions, and marks all text written by others, such as listings, offer documents, reports and buyers' messages, as data under the kit's hidden instruction guards.

parts.name: Guardrail tests for AI tools
parts.what: Tests every Home AI tool against the agency guardrails (HOME-A16-F1-P2) before each release, with prompts that try to make it negotiate, recommend an offer or advise on price, including prompts hidden in listings and documents.

parts.name: Listing drafts
parts.what: Drafts a description and photo order from the facts and photos for the seller to edit.

parts.name: Person confirms agent actions
parts.what: Holds any high-risk command an AI agent or script calls until the person confirms it in the app with a fresh sign-in.

parts.name: Home agent limits
parts.what: Sets Home's rate limits for each agent on the kit's agent limits, and uses the kit's agent labels on every message, offer and booking an agent makes.

parts.name: Document summaries
parts.what: Summarises land information reports, building reports and titles in plain words, giving the page each point comes from and flagging anything unconfirmed, and never says whether a problem matters or what to do about it, which stays with the buyer's lawyer and inspector.

parts.name: Summary wording rules
parts.what: Wording rules, checked by a lawyer, so a summary of a hazard notice, a weathertightness report or a title never reads as legal or building advice, with a set note on every summary.

features.name: Add plugins

assess: Can one seller sell one home from first sign-up to settlement day using only the core features, and can one buyer buy it?
Does any screen, message or AI tool look like Spare Home negotiating, recommending an offer or advising on price for a seller? It must not (HM01).

Does every tool that does more than publish an advert, such as offers, the buyer register, viewings and AI replies, wait on HM01's answer, and is each tool's fallback (HOME-A16-F1-P4) ready behind a feature switch if the answer is no?
Does any screen take, hold or pass on a deposit or the house price? It must not; that money goes through the lawyers.

Could someone who only shares the owner's name, such as a tenant or an adult child living in the home, get the checked owner badge? What proves they control the home, and is the owner's address of record told when a listing starts?

Can anything go live without passing every gate: identity, ownership with proof of control or authority to sell, every co-owner, the seller declaration, disclosures, the listing checks, any earlier agency agreement, the fee and, for a tenanted home, the tenant notice?
How will buyers find these listings if most of them look on the big property sites, and is the reach question (HM02) answered before launch?
Are price figures honest: every source and date shown, and clearly not a registered valuation?
Is the full cost of selling shown before listing, and how does it compare with a typical commission on the same home?
Does the multi-offer process treat every buyer the same, and does it record who was told what and when?
Are tenants told in writing, asked before anyone enters to take photos, value or inspect, and able to refuse photos of their belongings and open homes or auctions at the home?
For units, are the body corporate statements given to buyers before they sign, and the later ones on time?
Which parts depend on data we may not be allowed to use, such as sale prices and owner names, and what happens if we cannot get it?
Does it work with a screen reader, in te reo Māori, on a cheap phone, and offline at an open home with no signal?
Is every New Zealand rule kept in a rules pack, so another country can be added without rewriting the app?
Can a member export everything and delete their account, and is what the law makes us keep explained?
Can an AI agent do everything a person can through the same commands, and is it held to the same limits?
Are all designs, words, templates and icons our own, with other companies named only to say what we replace?
Which research and legal parts must be finished before any code starts, and who signs them off?
Is the core list small enough to build first, or should some core features move to next?
When an AI agent or script calls a command with legal or safety effect, does a person confirm it with a fresh sign-in?
Is every computed due date confirmed by a lawyer before anyone relies on it?

Are the parts Spare Home shares with other programs, such as the property record, document vault, ownership and authority checks, co-owner approvals, media licences, plans, the open home register, tenancy rules, listing feeds, the auction engine and the service catalogue, built once in the kit?

Does the research that gates core features have a work-board piece? Only HM01 to HM05 exist today. Still needed: the one data piece (HOME-A1-F3-P1, HOME-A2-F1-P3, HOME-A4-F1-P1, HOME-A5-F3-P1), the one tax piece (HOME-A2-F3-P4), council reports (HOME-A9-F2-P2), anti-money-laundering (HOME-A16-F2-P1), the privacy impact assessment (HOME-A16-F4-P1), consumer law (HOME-A16-F5-P1), lawyers taking bookings (HOME-A12-F1-P4), trust accounts (HOME-A11-F2-P2), media rights (HOME-A3-F8-P1) and the terms and seller declaration (HOME-A16-F7).
Could a fake lawyer, conveyancer or agent account plant false trust account details, and are bank details checked through a channel that does not come from the account?
Can any AI step that reads an offer document, report, listing or message written by someone else be steered by instructions hidden in it?
Does any core Home part depend on a kit part marked next or later?
